questions.q: By default, can a Script Include in one scope be called from a different scope?
options: Only on Sub-production instances
Only Global-scope Script Includes can be called from other scopes
Yes, every Script Include is callable from any scope automatically
No — access is closed by default, and must be explicitly opened by one of two real mechanisms
questions.explain: Scope isolates access as well as naming — ServiceNow assumes isolation unless a developer explicitly opens a door.

questions.q: What does setting a Script Include's "Accessible from" field to "All application scopes" do?
options: Grants access to exactly one named scope only
Deletes the Script Include from its original scope
Has no real effect on who can call the Script Include
Opens that Script Include's entire API to every scope on the instance, with no record of which scope actually uses it
questions.explain: It's a broad, instance-wide grant — the mechanism of last resort for genuinely generic, non-sensitive utility code.

questions.q: What is a Cross-Scope Access Control record, and where is it stored?
options: A setting that disables all Script Includes in a scope
A field on the sys_scope table that lists every scope on the instance
A targeted record in sys_scope_privilege granting one specific scope access to one specific target in another scope
A record that merges two scopes into one
questions.explain: sys_scope_privilege records are least-privilege and auditable — naming exactly which scope can reach exactly what.

questions.q: Why does ServiceNow recommend Cross-Scope Access Control over broadly setting "Accessible from" to all scopes?
options: Because Cross-Scope Access Control requires no configuration at all
Because "Accessible from" has been removed from newer ServiceNow versions
Because it's auditable and least-privilege — it names exactly which scope was granted access to exactly what
Because it's the only mechanism that actually works
questions.explain: Anyone reviewing the instance can see exactly which scope was granted access and why, instead of a blanket, untracked opening.

questions.q: What's a reasonable way to decide between the two cross-scope mechanisms for a given Script Include?
options: Flip a coin, since both mechanisms behave identically
Always use "All application scopes" since it's simpler to set up
Use "All application scopes" for genuinely generic, non-sensitive utilities; use a targeted Cross-Scope Access Control grant for anything touching real business data or security logic
Always use Cross-Scope Access Control, even for Global-scope code with no cross-scope callers
questions.explain: The decision hinges on sensitivity and whether you'd want an auditable record of exactly who can call the API.
